section: Science · Ch — Force, Motion, Work & Energy
subject: Science
stem: A wheelbarrow, where the load sits between the wheel (fulcrum) and the handles (effort), is an example of which class of lever?

options.option_text: Class II lever (load between fulcrum and effort)
Class I lever (fulcrum between load and effort)
Class III lever (effort between fulcrum and load)

explanation: In a Class II lever, the load lies between the fulcrum and the effort (as in a wheelbarrow or nutcracker) — this arrangement always provides a mechanical advantage greater than 1, making heavy loads easier to lift.

section: Science · Ch — Force, Motion, Work & Energy
subject: Science
stem: A pair of tweezers, or the human forearm lifting a weight (elbow = fulcrum, biceps = effort, hand = load), is an example of which class of lever, where the effort lies between the fulcrum and the load?
explanation: In a Class III lever, the effort is applied between the fulcrum and the load — this sacrifices mechanical advantage (needs more effort than the load) in exchange for greater speed/range of motion, as seen in tweezers or the human forearm.
